Summary Description: Hairong Song is a psychology researcher at the University of Oklahoma whose work spans health psychology, cultural psychology, and advanced statistical methods for behavioral science. Across collaborations on five distinct studies, Song integrates cultural constructs (such as feminine honor) with health behaviors (HPV vaccination intentions, smoking trajectories) while employing rigorous longitudinal and cross-cultural methodologies. Methodologically, Song contributions include mediation analyses with bootstrapping, multi-group measurement invariance, GLMMs with sophisticated variable selection, and model-based clustering of intensive longitudinal data, complemented by ranking-based approaches to predictor importance. The work leverages diverse data sources and tools (SPSS, R, Mplus, Python, TensorFlow) and emphasizes reproducibility through publicly available code and transparent analytic pipelines. Collectively, Song’s research advances theoretical understanding of how culture and gender intersect with health behaviors and demonstrates robust, scalable statistical approaches applicable to large-scale health and social data.
